independent.summary: The test 'the last owner re-asserted as owner is a 200, not the floor' claims in its comment that spreading the floor unconditionally would make this request a 409, but it would not: an unconditional `notTheLastOwner(owner)` makes the $elemMatch+floor filter match nothing (owners=[owner], so neither `|owners \ {owner}| >= 1` nor `|owners| == 0` holds), the no-match branch re-reads the member, finds them still `owner`, and answers the same `200 {role:'owner'}` with the same stored role. Only a log line differs, so the test passes with or without the `role === 'owner' ? {} :` conditional and does not pin the behaviour it says it pins.

triageGrades.reason: The diff rewrites an owner-gated membership-role endpoint and puts the last-owner authorization floor into a new write filter, so authorization/permission logic is squarely touched.
No credentials, tokens, or config secrets appear anywhere in the diff.
Nothing in the diff touches billing, allowances, or usage metering.
The diff does add a new mutating write to the persisted `members` array (`$set` on `members.$[m].role`) where the branch previously wrote nothing, so a data-mutation path is genuinely touched.
No outbound calls or third-party integrations are involved; the only I/O is MongoDB.
Only route code, tests, api.md and the spec change — no version bump, migration, or deploy config.

summary: The local model found nothing and its one substantive triage call was defensible, but it missed the toothless floor-conditional sentinel test and wrongly judged an owner-gated role-management change as not touching auth.
